title: Introduce residency-attestor middleware, compact audit bloomfilter index, and KMS origin whitelist
author: Anika Rao
description:
Motivation: Customers need stricter proof that requests touching tenant data were evaluated against tenant residency constraints and that any KMS usage originates from approved provider endpoints. This PR introduces three coordinated pieces: 1) a Residency Attestor middleware that centralizes tenant residency checks and emits structured attestations into request context; 2) a compact, append-only Audit BloomFilter index to lower cost of residency/audit lookups while preserving strong tamper-evidence; and 3) a KMS Origin Whitelist enforcement layer that rejects KMS operations not matching tenant-approved origin attributes.

Summary of changes:
- residency attestor middleware at service/auth/rbacv2/residency_attestor.go which reads tenant metadata (preferred regions, geozone claims) and executes policy checks via the policy-engine facade; on success it attaches a signed residency attestation header (X-Residency-Attestation) to propagated requests and writes a small proof record to the audit index.
- audit bloomfilter index implemented under service/audit/bloom_index with a compact on-disk segment format and in-memory sliding window for recent writes; the structure is optimized for space and fast existence checks used by downstream compliance tools.
- kms origin whitelist at pkg/kms/origin_whitelist.go which validates incoming KMS provider claims (kms-provider, region, endpoint fingerprint) against tenant-scoped allowlists; integrates with operator-scoped overrides guarded by RBAC v2.
- new audit forwarder shim that batches BloomFilter delta writes and pushes compressed proof envelopes to the audit-backend.
- integration tests and unit tests added under test/integration/residency_attestor_test.go and service/audit/bloom_index_test.go.

Compatibility and rollout:
- Middleware is enabled behind a feature flag feature.residency_attestor (default off). We will enable for a small set of internal tenants first.
- BloomFilter index exposes a migration shim: existing audit-index consumers can query a compatibility endpoint (/audit/compat/exists) until they are migrated.
- KMS origin whitelist defaults to permissive mode unless tenant has an allowlist configured; enforcement is gated by feature.kms_origin_whitelist (default off) to avoid surprise failures.

Testing and validation:
- Local unit tests: 118 tests added/updated.
- Integration: simulated tenant with multi-region config validated attestation header round-trip and audit bloom index retention under 10k ops/min.
- Load impact: bloom index writer optimized with a background, sharded flush that keeps p99 write latency under 25ms for our canary dataset.

Checklist: 
- [x] Residency attestor implementation
- [x] Compact bloom index and on-disk format documented in comments
- [x] KMS origin whitelist enforcement hook
- [x] Integration tests and CI coverage
- [x] Feature flags for safe rollout

Notes: This PR focuses on enforcement primitives and a compact proof store. Follow-up PRs will: provide operator UI to manage KMS allowlists per tenant, add audit search adapters that map BloomFilter hits back to canonical records, and wire attestation signing to HSM for tenants requiring non-repudiation.

release_notes:
- Added Residency Attestor middleware that emits per-request attestations and performs tenant residency checks.
- Introduced a compact Audit BloomFilter index for efficient existence checks and lower storage costs.
- Added KMS Origin Whitelist enforcement to validate KMS provider origin attributes against tenant allowlists.
- All features are behind feature flags for staged rollout.
